answer: Each identity may announce only one public network origin. Names that share a prefix, an ASN, or a nearly identical path from several looking glasses are merged into one vote. Each epoch, random vantage points require a live, signed echo from that origin inside a short window; a missed or colliding announcement earns nothing. A gale of keys cannot hide in one meadow of address space, and aliases that wander off a shared route still collapse, so a farm must obtain and keep a distinct, routinely announced prefix for every name.
